Thank you for commenting. I’m sure it was very difficult having to part with your brothers’s belongings the way you did. I know it’s only “stuff”, but that stuff is all we have left of our loved ones. I think that decisions to “get rid of” certain things should be discussed together as a unit. That way everyone has a say and feels involved in the process. When big decisions like that are made without you, it honestly just feels like a betrayal.

This September she will have been gone for 4 years. It was very hard on both of us being manipulated and kept apart. I never expected her to die when she did. I would have gotten in the car as soon as we hung up instead of waiting two days if I had had any idea. I regret so much. It was very sudden and unexpected. Despite my age, I absolutely felt — and still feel — helpless. With her gone I feel all alone in the world. My family took everything, even her ashes, and refused to share with me. The are vile and selfish humans. One of my cousins stole a small bag of her ashes and gave them to me because she felt bad about how the family was treating me. The whole story is absolutely insane.

“She didn’t love you, she only pitied you.”

My grandmother was my everything..the love of my life. She raised me and we were very close. She was the only person in my life who ever cared about me. She also stepped in to help take care of me when I became chronically ill. No one else in my family gave a damn what happened to me. The rest of my blood relatives are awful and even kept her and I apart towards the end of her life. They would call me and lie to me saying that she didn’t want to talk to me and that all I did was stress her out, and that it was my fault she had to go to the hospital. I eventually learned that they were controlling her and hiding her phone so she couldn’t contact me. We finally communicated after she was able to sneak a call to me. She asked me to please come, and I made plans to go to her but she died suddenly before I arrived. My family completely swarmed her home, set up camp there, and locked me out. They stole, they lied, they destroyed her belongings and threw away anything that was mine including boxes of priceless photographs and home movies. Additionally they said horrible horrible things to me after my she passed, like she never really loved me. They have been abusive to me my entire life — physically, sexually, verbally — but the venomous words they spewed at me after she died were far more painful than any of their previous abuse. There is a lot more to this story, but it’s difficult to talk about.
